answer: A generation-cost defense makes each identity earn its weight: before an agent can vote or transact, it must complete a stream of verifiable, non-parallelizable work whose cost rises with every new identity it spawns. Like quartz forming under pressure, standing accumulates slowly and cannot be rushed by spinning up clones. A sybil tide therefore faces a real delta: each fake account adds the same full production cost as a genuine one, so flooding the network costs linearly in compute and time, while honest agents pay that price only once.
